Lead poisoning. Unithiol may be used in lead poisoning, al- though other chelators are generally preferred (see Treatment of Adverse Effects under Lead, p.2332). In a study of 12 children1 it reduced lead concentrations in blood but did not affect the con- centrations of copper or zinc in plasma, although the urinary ex- cretion of lead, copper, and zinc was increased during treatment. 1. Chisolm JJ, Thomas DJ. Use of 2,3-dimercaptopropane-1-sul- fonate in treatment of lead poisoning in children. J Pharmacol Exp Ther 1985; 235: 665–9. Mercury poisoning. Unithiol is used in poisoning with mercu- ry and mercury salts (see Treatment of Adverse Effects under Mercury, p.2342) and has been given by various routes. In 7 pa- tients with poisoning due to mercury vapour or mercuric oxide, unithiol 100 mg given twice daily by mouth for up to 15 days enhanced urinary elimination of mercury;1 the urinary elimina- tion of copper and zinc was also increased in most patients and 2 developed skin rashes. A dose of 5 mg/kg intramuscularly three times daily, reduced to once daily by the third day of treatment, effectively reduced the half-life of mercury in the blood after poi- soning with methylmercury.2 A patient with severe mercuric chloride poisoning was treated successfully with unithiol given intravenously for 4 weeks, then orally for 3 weeks.3 Unithiol has also been used with haemofiltration in patients with inorganic mercury poisoning and acute renal failure.4,5 1.
